The fowler reveals that he was once a Brahmana who accidentally shot a sage while hunting with a king, and was cursed to be born a fowler in the Sudra class.

scenes.B03C214S01: The fowler urges the Brahmana to go home to his parents, then tells how he came to be a fowler after accidentally wounding a sage while hunting.

shots.B03C214S01H01: The fowler says the Brahmana was sent to him by the lady, scolds him for leaving his grieving parents to study without permission, and urges him to go home; the Brahmana thanks him and asks why such a virtuous man is a fowler.
shots.B03C214S01H02: The fowler reveals that he was once a Brahmana who, while hunting deer with a king, accidentally struck a sage, and the sage cursed him to be a fowler in the Sudra class.

B03C215.summary: The sage softens his curse, promising the fowler will stay pious, recall his past life and regain Brahmana status once the curse ends. The Brahmana tells him that character, not birth, makes a Brahmana, and the fowler teaches that wisdom and contentment overcome grief. The Brahmana then leaves to serve his own parents, and Yudhishthira says he is still eager for more of the teaching.

scenes.B03C215S01: The sage's curse is softened, the Brahmana praises the fowler's teaching on character and contentment, and he goes home to his parents, closing the story for Yudhishthira.

shots.B03C215S01H01: The fowler recounts that the sage, sparing him, promised he would stay pious and regain Brahmana status, and the Brahmana replies that a man's character, not his birth, makes him a Brahmana.
shots.B03C215S01H02: The fowler teaches that bodily ills need medicine and grief needs knowledge, and that contentment is the highest happiness, and the Brahmana praises him and takes his leave.
shots.B03C215S01H03: Markandeya says the Brahmana went home to care for his parents, and Yudhishthira declares he is not yet satisfied with the teaching.

B03C216.summary: Yudhishthira asks why the fire-god hid in water, why Angiras acted as fire, and how Kumara came to be called Agni's son. Markandeya tells how Agni grew depressed at Angiras's brilliance, and how Angiras persuaded him to resume his place, which led to the birth of Vrihaspati. The gods learned the mystery from Angiras, and Markandeya prepares to describe the sacred fires.

scenes.B03C216S01: Yudhishthira asks about the fire-god's withdrawal and the birth of Kumara, and Markandeya tells how Agni returned to his place after Angiras persuaded him.

shots.B03C216S01H01: Yudhishthira asks why the fire-god hid in water, why Angiras acted as fire, and how Kumara came to be called Agni's son, and Markandeya tells how Angiras persuaded the depressed Agni to resume his place and fathered Vrihaspati.

B03C217.summary: Markandeya lists the children that Angiras had with his wife Subha. The son Vrihaspati is named first, followed by several daughters, each named for a quality such as beauty, light or sacrifice.

scenes.B03C217S01: Markandeya lists Angiras's children by Subha, starting with his son Vrihaspati and several daughters, each named for a quality.

shots.B03C217S01H01: Markandeya names Angiras's son Vrihaspati and his several daughters, explaining how each got her name from a trait such as beauty, brightness or accepting oblations.

B03C218.summary: Markandeya lists the children of Vrihaspati and his wife Tara, who are themselves sacred fires. Each son has a name and a role, such as Sanju, Bharadwaja, Viswabhuk and Vadava, tied to particular sacrifices or functions. Swaha bears three sons linked to sattwa, rajas and tamas, which shows how the many fires arise from a single source.

scenes.B03C218S01: Markandeya traces the fire-deities descended from Vrihaspati, each named for a sacrificial role, with Swaha's three sons linked to the three qualities.

shots.B03C218S01H01: Markandeya names Vrihaspati's sons by Tara, each a fire with its own sacrificial role, and Swaha's three sons, linked to the three qualities.

B03C219.summary: A being born from a long penance, marked with five colours from five sages, goes on to create the fire of the manes, day and night, and many other beings. Among his creations are fifteen gods who obstruct sacrifices and must be appeased with hymns. The chapter closes with the father of this line, who is pleased with his sons.

scenes.B03C219S01: A being from Uktha's penance, marked with five colours, creates the fire of the manes, day and night, and the sacrifice-obstructing gods who must be appeased.

shots.B03C219S01H01: After Uktha's long penance, a radiant being with five colours arises from the sacred fires and five sages, and goes on to create the fire of the manes, day and night, many beings, and fifteen gods who obstruct sacrifices unless they are appeased.

B03C220.summary: Markandeya names many fires descended from Tapa and Bhanu, each with its own name and role in sacrifice, and the list shows how the fires multiply. He then gives the rites needed to correct the sacred fire when it is disturbed by death, contact with a menstruating woman, or other defilement.

scenes.B03C220S01: Markandeya names many fires descended from Tapa and Bhanu and lists the rites needed to correct the sacred fire when it is disturbed.

shots.B03C220S01H01: Markandeya lists more fire-gods, from Bharata and Siva to Bhanu's six sons, and then prescribes the rites that set right the sacred fire when it is disturbed, such as contact with a woman in her monthly course or the presence of death.

B03C221.summary: Markandeya tells how the fire Swaha hid in the sea to avoid defilement, and how the sage Atharvan, who carried the oblations for a time, gave up his body. From that body came metals and woods, and Atharvan later restored the fire. He then names the rivers that are said to be the mothers of the fires, and explains that all the fires are one.

scenes.B03C221S01: Markandeya tells how Swaha hid from defilement and how Atharvan restored him, then names the rivers said to be the mothers of the fires.

shots.B03C221S01H01: Markandeya tells how the fire Swaha hid in the sea to avoid defilement, and how the sage Atharvan, who carried the oblations, gave up his body, which yielded metals and woods, until Atharvan restored the fire.
shots.B03C221S01H02: Markandeya names a long list of rivers as the mothers of the fires, and says that all the fires are one, arising from Brahma's spirit and from the sage Atri.

B03C222.summary: Markandeya begins the story of Kartikeya, who is to lead the gods. Indra, looking for a leader, hears a woman's cries in the Manasa mountains and finds the Asura Kesin trying to seize her. Indra drives Kesin off with his thunderbolt, and then asks the woman who she is.

scenes.B03C222S01: Indra, seeking a leader for the gods, rescues a woman from the Asura Kesin in the Manasa mountains and drives the Asura off.

shots.B03C222S01H01: Markandeya introduces Kartikeya's story and tells how Indra, seeking a leader for the gods, rescues a woman from the Asura Kesin in the Manasa mountains, cutting down his mace and rock with his thunderbolt.

B03C223.summary: The woman, Devasena, daughter of Prajapati, says her sister was carried off by Kesin and asks Indra to find her a champion husband. Indra reads omens in the union of Sun, Moon and Agni, hoping a son of Soma or Agni could be her husband, and Brahma approves his plan. Meanwhile the fire Adbhuta, overcome by desire for the Rishis' wives, resolves to look at them only as his household fire, and Swaha schemes to win him in disguise.

scenes.B03C223S01: Devasena asks for a champion husband, Indra reads omens and wins Brahma's approval, and the fire Adbhuta, aroused by the Rishis' wives, is pursued in disguise by Swaha.

shots.B03C223S01H01: Devasena, daughter of Prajapati, says her sister was carried off by Kesin and asks Indra to find her a husband who is devoted to Brahma and able to conquer every class of being.
shots.B03C223S01H02: Indra reads omens in the conjunction of Sun, Moon and Agni and goes to Brahma, who approves; meanwhile the fire Adbhuta, seeing the Rishis' wives, is struck by desire and resolves to look at them only as his household fire.
shots.B03C223S01H03: Frustrated and lovesick, the Adbhuta fire goes into a forest to die, and Swaha, who loves him, plans to take the form of the seven Rishis' wives to win him.

B03C224.summary: Swaha, disguised as Siva the wife of Angiras, woos Agni by claiming the other Rishis' wives sent her, and after their union she flies to the White Mountain and casts his seed into a golden lake. From it a six-faced child, Skanda, is born, who shows his might by tearing a mountain and roaring until the three worlds tremble. The gods and creatures then seek his protection.

scenes.B03C224S01: Swaha, disguised as Siva, seduces Agni and casts his seed into a lake, from which the six-faced Skanda is born and displays his power.

shots.B03C224S01H01: Swaha, in the disguise of Siva, wife of Angiras, approaches Agni, declares her love, and says she was sent by the wives of the other Rishis.
shots.B03C224S01H02: Agni asks how she knew of his love, and how the Rishis' wives could have known it.
shots.B03C224S01H03: Swaha replies that the wives read his mind by signs and sent her, and urges him to act quickly because her sisters-in-law are waiting.
shots.B03C224S01H04: Agni, delighted, marries Swaha in Siva's guise, and she then decides to take a bird's form so that no one will slander the Brahmana ladies.
shots.B03C224S01H05: Swaha flies to the White Mountain, throws Agni's seed into a golden lake, and a six-faced child, Skanda, is born, grows quickly, and fights and tears a mountain, leaving the gods and creatures to seek his protection.

B03C225.summary: The birth causes strange omens, and the seven Rishis divorce six of their wives, keeping only Arundhati, after Swaha reveals to Skanda that she is his mother. Viswamitra clears the wives of blame and performs the child's rites, though the Rishis still abandon their spouses. The gods urge Indra to kill Skanda, but he hesitates, and the Mothers take the child as their own and nurse him.

scenes.B03C225S01: The omens follow Skanda's birth, Swaha is revealed as mother, six wives are divorced, Viswamitra performs the rites, and the gods' plot to kill Skanda is set aside as the Mothers adopt him.

shots.B03C225S01H01: The birth brings strange omens, Swaha reveals to Skanda that she is his mother, and the seven Rishis divorce six of their wives, keeping only Arundhati.
shots.B03C225S01H02: Viswamitra, who had followed Agni, tells the Rishis their wives are innocent, performs the child's rites, and promotes Skanda's worship, though the Rishis still abandon their spouses.
shots.B03C225S01H03: The gods urge Indra to kill Skanda, but he hesitates, and the Mothers, awed by the child's power, adopt him and nurse him while Agni comes disguised as a trader with toys.

B03C226.summary: Indra marches out with the gods and their armies to destroy Skanda. Skanda's fiery breath burns the forces, and when the gods desert Indra he hurls his thunderbolt, which pierces Skanda and gives birth to a new being, Visakha. Indra then begs Skanda's protection, and peace returns.

scenes.B03C226S01: Indra advances against Skanda, is driven back by his fire, and then pierces him with the thunderbolt, from whose wound Visakha is born.

shots.B03C226S01H01: Indra and the gods advance against Skanda, whose fiery breath burns the forces, and when the gods desert Indra he hurls his thunderbolt, from which a new being named Visakha springs.

B03C227.summary: The wound from the thunderbolt gives rise to a host of followers, male and female, who adopt Visakha as their father. The seven Mothers and their son Sisu are named, and Skanda is called the father of the Kumaras because of these followers. The battle is said to have been fought on the sixth day of the lunar fortnight.

scenes.B03C227S01: The wound yields a host of followers, the Mothers and Sisu are named, and Skanda is called the father of the Kumaras.

shots.B03C227S01H01: The wound gives rise to a host of followers, including Bhadrasakha, and the seven Mothers and their son Sisu are named, which is why Skanda is called father of the Kumaras.

B03C228.summary: Skanda, handsome and blessed with fortune, is urged by the Rishis to become Indra, but he declines the sovereignty and serves Indra instead. Indra asks Skanda to lead the celestial forces, and Skanda is anointed commander, honoured as the son of Rudra. He is then married to Devasena, whom Indra brings to him, and the day of his anointing is remembered as a sacred day.

scenes.B03C228S01: Skanda is urged to become Indra, declines, and Indra asks him to lead the gods' forces.
scenes.B03C228S02: Skanda is anointed commander, honoured as the son of Rudra, and married to Devasena, and the sacred days of his anointing and victory are named.

shots.B03C228S01H01: Skanda's beauty and good fortune are described, and the Maharshis urge him to become Indra, lord of the three worlds.
shots.B03C228S01H02: Indra offers to anoint Skanda as lord that very day.
shots.B03C228S01H03: Skanda declines the sovereignty and says he would rather serve as Indra's humble servant.
shots.B03C228S01H04: Indra explains that if he stepped aside, the gods would split into factions and war would follow, which Skanda would surely win.
shots.B03C228S01H05: Skanda replies that Indra remains his sovereign and asks what commands he is to obey.
shots.B03C228S02H01: Indra asks Skanda to take up leadership of the celestial forces, if that is truly what he wishes.
shots.B03C228S02H02: Skanda asks to be anointed leader for the destruction of the Danavas, the good of the gods, and the protection of cows and Brahmanas.
shots.B03C228S02H03: Skanda is anointed by Indra and the gods, Rudra gives him a golden wreath, and Markandeya explains why he is called the son of Rudra.
shots.B03C228S02H04: Skanda is dressed in red with a red cock as his emblem, and his inborn virtues, including devotion to Brahmanas, are listed as the gods rejoice.
shots.B03C228S02H05: Indra brings Devasena, whom he had rescued, and she is married to Skanda, and the fifth and sixth days of the lunar month are named after his anointing and victory.

B03C229.summary: The six wives of the Rishis, cast out on a rumour that they bore Skanda, ask him to adopt them as his mothers, and he agrees. The mother goddesses then ask him to take their place and give them back their offspring, and Skanda grants them other offspring in exchange, so they may protect children. He sets them and a host of spirits to trouble children until they reach sixteen, and Markandeya lists the spirits that afflict men after that age.

scenes.B03C229S01: The cast-off Rishis' wives ask Skanda to adopt them, Indra and Vinata seek honour from him, and the Mothers claim to be his mothers as well.
scenes.B03C229S02: The Mothers ask Skanda to replace the earlier mother goddesses and to let them devour rivals' children, and Skanda gives them other offspring on condition that they protect children.
scenes.B03C229S03: Skanda sets the Mothers to afflict children until sixteen, and Markandeya lists the spirits that trouble children and adults.

shots.B03C229S01H01: The six Rishis' wives, cast out on a rumour, come to Skanda and ask him to adopt them and clear their name.
shots.B03C229S01H02: Skanda agrees to accept them as his mothers and promises them their desires.
shots.B03C229S01H03: Indra notes that the star Abhijit has left its place and that Krittika must fill it, and Vinata asks Skanda to honour her as a son.
shots.B03C229S01H04: Skanda agrees to honour Vinata as a mother, and says she will live with him.
shots.B03C229S01H05: The great Mothers say they are already mothers of all creatures, but want to be Skanda's mothers too and asks him to honour them.
shots.B03C229S02H01: Skanda tells the Mothers they are all his mothers and asks what he can do to please them.
shots.B03C229S02H02: The Mothers ask to replace the earlier mother goddesses in worship and to recover the offspring taken from them.
shots.B03C229S02H03: Skanda refuses to return what was given away, but offers other offspring instead.
shots.B03C229S02H04: The Mothers ask to live with Skanda and devour the offspring of rival mothers and their guardians.
shots.B03C229S02H05: Skanda grants them progeny, but asks them to protect the children and calls the topic painful.
shots.B03C229S03H01: The Mothers agree to protect the children as Skanda asks, and ask to stay with him always.
shots.B03C229S03H02: Skanda says the Mothers shall afflict children until their sixteenth year, and that they will be worshipped with a fierce spirit.
shots.B03C229S03H03: Markandeya lists the evil spirits that trouble children and the unborn until age sixteen, including the Skandapasmara and the Mothers Putana, Revati and Sarama, and says they are appeased by worship.
shots.B03C229S03H04: Markandeya lists the spirits that drive men mad after sixteen, including the celestial, ancestral, Siddha, Rakshasa, Gandharva, Pisacha and Yaksha spirits, and says that self-controlled men are free from them.

B03C230.summary: Swaha asks Skanda to grant her union with Agni, and he decrees that offerings made through Agni will carry her name. Brahma then sends Skanda to visit his father Mahadeva, and the chapter describes the spirits, bells and banners of Skanda and the grand procession of Mahadeva's army. An Asura attack follows, in which Mahisha seizes Rudra's chariot until Skanda slays him, and Skanda then routs the Danavas. Markandeya closes with a long list of Skanda's names and a prayer, promising fame, wealth and salvation to those who recite them.

scenes.B03C230S01: Swaha asks Skanda to grant her union with Agni, and he links her name to offerings made through Agni.
scenes.B03C230S02: Brahma sends Skanda to his father, and Markandeya describes the spirits, the bells and banners, and the grand procession of Mahadeva's army.
scenes.B03C230S03: Skanda is dismissed, omens appear, and the Asuras attack; Indra rallies the gods, and Mahisha seizes Rudra's chariot until Skanda kills him.
scenes.B03C230S04: Skanda routs the Danavas and is praised by Indra; Markandeya closes the story with a list of Skanda's names and a prayer to him.

shots.B03C230S01H01: Swaha, having been given these powers, appears before Skanda, calls him her natural son, and asks him to grant her happiness.
shots.B03C230S01H02: Skanda asks what kind of happiness she wishes.
shots.B03C230S01H03: Swaha says she has loved the Fire-god since her youth and asks to live forever with him as his wife.
shots.B03C230S01H04: Skanda decrees that offerings made through Agni will carry Swaha's name, so she will always be joined with him.
shots.B03C230S01H05: Pleased, Swaha honours Skanda in return, along with her husband Agni.
shots.B03C230S02H01: Brahma tells Skanda to visit his father Mahadeva, explaining that Rudra and Agni, Uma and Swaha made him invincible and that his fierce followers came from Rudra's seed.
shots.B03C230S02H02: Markandeya describes how the five classes of spirits should be worshipped, gives the origin of Skanda's two bells and red banners, and pictures the White Mountain full of gods and celestial creatures.
shots.B03C230S02H03: Mahadeva and Parvati set out in a lion-drawn chariot, with the gods, spirits and celestial powers marching in a great procession, and Pingala leads as standard-bearer.
shots.B03C230S02H04: Skanda, leader of the army, follows Mahadeva, who asks him to command the seventh corps.
shots.B03C230S02H05: Skanda accepts the command and asks whether anything else needs doing.
shots.B03C230S03H01: Rudra tells Skanda that he will always find him on the field of action, and that devotion to him brings welfare.
shots.B03C230S03H02: Maheswara embraces Skanda and sends him off, and then prodigies disturb the gods.
shots.B03C230S03H03: Terrible omens appear, a vast Asura host attacks the celestial army with weapons and rocks, and Indra rallies the wavering gods.
shots.B03C230S03H04: Encouraged by Indra, the gods charge the Danavas and inflict heavy losses, but the Danavas soon regain the upper hand.
shots.B03C230S03H05: The Danava Mahisha crushes ten thousand gods with a rock and seizes Rudra's chariot, and Skanda rushes in and cuts off Mahisha's head with his spear.
shots.B03C230S04H01: Skanda's spear returns to his hand after killing thousands, his followers devour the Danavas, Indra praises him, and the reader of this story is promised prosperity.
shots.B03C230S04H02: Yudhishthira asks Markandeya for the different names by which Skanda is known across the three worlds.
shots.B03C230S04H03: Markandeya lists more than fifty names of Kartikeya, each with a meaning, and says that reciting them brings fame, wealth and salvation.
shots.B03C230S04H04: Markandeya prays to Guha, calling him devoted to Brahma, the six-flamed fire, the seasons and the universe, and many other names and forms.
shots.B03C230S04H05: Markandeya promises that whoever reads, tells or hears this story of Skanda's birth gains wealth, long life, children, victory and Skanda's companionship.

B03C231.summary: Satyabhama asks Draupadi what secret keeps the five Pandavas so obedient to her, suggesting charms, drugs or vows. Draupadi rejects such charms as wicked and describes her humble, devoted service to her husbands, to Kunti, and in running the household, servants and treasury. Satyabhama apologises for her jest, saying such talk arises naturally between friends.

scenes.B03C231S01: Satyabhama asks Draupadi how she wins her husbands' obedience, and Draupadi replies that it comes from humble, dutiful service rather than charms, listing her household duties; Satyabhama then apologises.

shots.B03C231S01H01: A heading naming the section as the dialogue between Draupadi and Satyabhama.
shots.B03C231S01H02: Vaisampayana describes Draupadi and Satyabhama meeting after a long time, and Satyabhama asks how Draupadi keeps the Pandavas so obedient, listing possible charms, drugs or vows.
shots.B03C231S01H03: Draupadi calls such charms the practice of wicked women, describes her humble service to her husbands and to Kunti, and lists how she manages the palace servants, the feeding of Brahmanas and the treasury.
shots.B03C231S01H04: Satyabhama asks Draupadi's forgiveness for her jest, saying such talk arises naturally among friends.

B03C232.summary: Draupadi advises Satyabhama on how to win Krishna's heart through honest, humble service rather than deceit. She urges her to greet him promptly, keep his secrets, avoid his enemies and wicked women, and adorn herself for him. The advice presents devotion to the husband as the source of reputation, prosperity and heaven.

scenes.B03C232S01: Draupadi gives Satyabhama practical advice on winning and keeping her husband's love through devoted service, discretion and good company.

shots.B03C232S01H01: Draupadi advises Satyabhama to win Krishna through devoted, humble service and discretion, such as rising promptly to greet him, keeping his secrets, avoiding his enemies, and adorning herself for him.

B03C233.summary: Krishna takes leave of the Pandavas and the Brahmanas and calls for Satyabhama. Satyabhama comforts Draupadi, foreseeing the Pandavas' return to power and the ruin of the Kuru sons, and reports that the Pandava sons are well and cared for in Dwaraka. She then circles Draupadi, mounts Krishna's car, and they leave for his city.

scenes.B03C233S01: Krishna takes leave of the Pandavas, and Satyabhama comforts Draupadi with news of the Pandava sons in Dwaraka and of their future victory.

shots.B03C233S01H01: Krishna takes leave of the Pandavas and the Brahmanas, and Satyabhama comforts Draupadi, foreseeing the Pandavas' return to power and the ruin of the Kuru sons, and reporting that the Pandava sons are well in Dwaraka.
shots.B03C233S01H02: Satyabhama circles Draupadi, mounts Krishna's car, and Krishna, comforting Draupadi with a smile, returns with her to his own city.

B03C234.summary: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did in the Dwaita forest after they reached the lake. A talkative Brahmana who has been visiting them carries news of their misery to Dhritarashtra, who laments their plight at length, blaming fate and the deceit of his own sons. Sakuni then tells Duryodhana in private, and Duryodhana, though foolish, is grieved.

scenes.B03C234S01: Janamejaya asks about the Pandavas in the forest, a Brahmana brings news of their suffering to Dhritarashtra, who laments, and Sakuni reports the king's words to Duryodhana.

shots.B03C234S01H01: A heading naming the section as the Ghosha-yatra Parva.
shots.B03C234S01H02: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did after reaching the Dwaita lake and enduring the heat and cold of the forest.
shots.B03C234S01H03: The Pandavas settle in the Dwaita forest, a talkative Brahmana carries news of their misery to Dhritarashtra, and the king laments their hardships at length, blaming fate and his own role.
shots.B03C234S01H04: Sakuni, son of Suvala, tells Duryodhana in private what the king said, and Duryodhana, though foolish, is grieved.

B03C235.summary: Sakuni, prompted by Karna, urges Duryodhana to rule the earth without rival and to visit the Pandavas in their Dwaita forest home, flaunting his wealth before them. He argues that the happiness of seeing a defeated enemy surpasses any gift or kingdom, and suggests Duryodhana's wives mock Draupadi in her poverty. When they finish, Karna and Sakuni fall silent.

scenes.B03C235S01: Sakuni and Karna urge Duryodhana to go and gloat over the exiled Pandavas, and when they finish they fall silent.

shots.B03C235S01H01: Sakuni, with Karna's support, urges Duryodhana to rule without rival and go to see the Pandavas at Dwaitavana, displaying his prosperity to their suffering.
shots.B03C235S01H02: Vaisampayana says that Karna and Sakuni fell silent after their speech was over.

B03C236.summary: Duryodhana is pleased by Karna's words but doubts that his father will let him go to the Pandavas' forest, since he longs to see them humbled and suffering. Karna proposes a pretext: inspecting the royal cattle stations at Dwaitavana, a plan Sakuni also endorses. The three agree to put the idea to King Dhritarashtra.

scenes.B03C236S01: Duryodhana doubts he can win permission to visit the Pandavas, and Karna and Sakuni agree on the cattle-inspection pretext.

shots.B03C236S01H01: Duryodhana is pleased by Karna's words, but doubts his father will allow him to visit the Pandavas, and says he longs to see them humbled in the woods.
shots.B03C236S01H02: Karna proposes that they go to Dwaitavana under the pretext of supervising the royal cattle stations, and Sakuni agrees that this will work.
shots.B03C236S01H03: The three laugh together, shake hands, and go to see the king.

B03C237.summary: Karna and Sakuni ask Dhritarashtra to let Duryodhana go to the cattle stations at Dwaitavana for the hunt and the herd count. The king warns that the Pandavas are near, that their anger and Draupadi's power could harm the Kauravas, and that Duryodhana should not go himself. Sakuni reassures him, and the king grudgingly gives permission for a large party to set out.

scenes.B03C237S01: Dhritarashtra is asked to permit a cattle-inspection trip, warns of the Pandavas, and grudgingly lets Duryodhana go with a large following.

shots.B03C237S01H01: The three greet Dhritarashtra, a cowherd named Samanga speaks of the cattle, and Karna and Sakuni ask leave for Duryodhana to inspect the herds and go hunting.
shots.B03C237S01H02: Dhritarashtra warns that the Pandavas are near the cattle stations and that their anger and Draupadi's power could injure the Kauravas, so he advises that Duryodhana should not go himself.
shots.B03C237S01H03: Sakuni reassures the king that Yudhishthira will not be angry and that the Kauravas have no wish to meet the Pandavas.
shots.B03C237S01H04: Dhritarashtra reluctantly permits the trip, and Duryodhana sets out with a large host and camps four miles from the lake.

B03C238.summary: Duryodhana inspects and marks his cattle, and he and his court enjoy hunting, music, dancing and generous gifts in the woods. When he tries to set up pleasure-houses by the lake at Dwaitavana, where Yudhishthira is performing a daily rite, he finds that the Gandharva king Chitrasena has come there for sport and barred the way. The Gandharvas mock the Kuru messengers and refuse to yield.

scenes.B03C238S01: Duryodhana inspects his cattle and enjoys the woods, then finds the lake at Dwaitavana blocked by Chitrasena's Gandharvas, who spurn his messengers.

shots.B03C238S01H01: Duryodhana inspects and marks his cattle at the stations, and then enjoys songs, dances and generous gifts with his attendants and ladies.
shots.B03C238S01H02: He hunts widely and reaches the lake where Yudhishthira is performing a daily rite with Draupadi, but when his men try to enter, Gandharvas under Chitrasena block the way and mock the Kuru messengers, who turn back.
shots.B03C238S01H03: A heading marking the start of Section CCXXXIX.

B03C239.summary: Duryodhana orders his soldiers to punish the Gandharvas, and the Kuru army attacks the forest. Chitrasena rallies his host, and the Kuru army flees, leaving only Karna standing and fighting hard. The Gandharvas use illusions to overwhelm the Kauravas, and Karna's chariot is broken until he escapes on Vikarna's car.

scenes.B03C239S01: The Kuru soldiers attack the Gandharvas and are routed, and Karna fights alone until his chariot is broken and he escapes.

shots.B03C239S01H01: Duryodhana orders an attack, the Kuru army charges into the forest, Chitrasena's Gandharvas rush at them, and the Kuru army flees, leaving only Karna to slaughter many before the Gandharvas overwhelm the field.
shots.B03C239S01H02: Chitrasena uses illusions to overpower the Kauravas, only Karna, Duryodhana and Sakuni keep fighting, and the Gandharvas break Karna's chariot until he escapes on Vikarna's car.

B03C240.summary: The Gandharvas rout the Kauravas and seize Duryodhana, Dussasana and the royal ladies, and the fleeing soldiers appeal to the Pandavas to rescue them. Bhima answers with sarcasm, saying the Kauravas are now paying for their deceit and that the Pandavas are not wicked. Yudhishthira reproves him, telling him this is no time for cruel words.

scenes.B03C240S01: Duryodhana and the Kaurava party are seized by the Gandharvas, and the fleeing soldiers appeal to the Pandavas, while Bhima mocks them and Yudhishthira reproves him.

shots.B03C240S01H01: After the rout Duryodhana is captured by Chitrasena, Dussasana and others are seized, the royal ladies are taken, and the fleeing soldiers appeal to the Pandavas to rescue the captives.
shots.B03C240S01H02: Bhima, speaking sarcastically, says the Kauravas are now paying the price of their deceit, and insists the Pandavas are not wicked.
shots.B03C240S01H03: Yudhishthira reproves Bhima, saying this is not the time for cruel words.

B03C241.summary: Yudhishthira rebukes Bhima and urges his brothers to rescue Duryodhana, arguing that family honour must be defended even against kinsmen and that an insult from a stranger must be avenged. He tells them to try conciliation first and to use force only if the Gandharva king refuses. Arjuna pledges to free the Kauravas or drink the Gandharva king's blood, and the Kauravas regain their spirit.

scenes.B03C241S01: Yudhishthira urges his brothers to rescue Duryodhana, first by conciliation and then by force if needed, and Arjuna pledges to do so, restoring the Kauravas' spirits.

shots.B03C241S01H01: Yudhishthira rebukes Bhima and urges his brothers to rescue Duryodhana and defend the honour of the family, first by conciliation and then by force if necessary.
shots.B03C241S01H02: Arjuna pledges to free the Kauravas or make the earth drink the Gandharva king's blood, and the Kauravas regain their spirit.

B03C242.summary: The Pandavas arm themselves in gold-trimmed mail and march toward the Gandharvas, and the Kuru army cheers them on. Arjuna asks the Gandharvas to release Duryodhana, but they reply that they obey only Indra. When Arjuna threatens to free the Kauravas by force, the two sides begin a fierce battle.

scenes.B03C242S01: The Pandavas arm and march out, Arjuna demands Duryodhana's release, the Gandharvas refuse, and battle begins.

shots.B03C242S01H01: The Pandavas arm in gold-trimmed mail and march to the Gandharvas, and when Arjuna asks them to free Duryodhana, they refuse, saying they obey only Indra, and battle begins.

B03C243.summary: The Gandharvas, far more numerous than the four Pandavas, press them hard. Arjuna's celestial weapons slaughter thousands and trap the Gandharvas who were carrying off the Kauravas. Chitrasena then vanishes by illusion, but Arjuna reveals him with a special weapon, and Chitrasena declares himself Arjuna's friend, after which the fighting stops.

scenes.B03C243S01: Arjuna and the Pandavas defeat the Gandharvas with celestial weapons, and when Chitrasena reveals himself as Arjuna's friend, the fighting stops.

shots.B03C243S01H01: The Pandavas battle the Gandharvas, Arjuna's weapons slaughter thousands and trap those carrying the Kauravas, and when Chitrasena hides by illusion Arjuna reveals him, and Chitrasena announces himself as Arjuna's friend, ending the battle.

B03C244.summary: Arjuna asks Chitrasena why he has punished the Kauravas, and Chitrasena explains that Duryodhana and Karna came to mock the exiles and that Indra ordered him to bring Duryodhana in chains. When Arjuna asks for Duryodhana's release, Chitrasena refuses, so the Gandharvas and Pandavas take the prisoners to Yudhishthira, who frees them and praises the Gandharvas. Yudhishthira then warns Duryodhana never to act rashly again and sends him home in shame.

scenes.B03C244S01: Arjuna and Chitrasena argue over the captives, Chitrasena explains the Kaurava plot, and the Gandharvas and Pandavas take the captives to Yudhishthira.
scenes.B03C244S02: The Gandharvas depart, Indra revives the slain, Yudhishthira warns Duryodhana against rash acts, and Duryodhana sets off for his capital in shame.

shots.B03C244S01H01: Arjuna asks Chitrasena why he has punished the Kauravas, and why Duryodhana and his wives were seized.
shots.B03C244S01H02: Chitrasena explains that Duryodhana and Karna came to mock the exiles, and that Indra ordered him to bring Duryodhana back in chains.
shots.B03C244S01H03: Arjuna asks Chitrasena to free Duryodhana, since he is their brother.
shots.B03C244S01H04: Chitrasena refuses, calling Duryodhana a vain and deceitful wretch, and says Yudhishthira must hear the whole matter first.
shots.B03C244S01H05: The Gandharvas and Pandavas go to Yudhishthira, who frees the Kauravas, praises the Gandharvas, and asks what he can do in return.
shots.B03C244S02H01: The Gandharvas leave with the Apsaras, Indra revives the slain Gandharvas, and Yudhishthira warns Duryodhana never to act rashly again and sends him home.
shots.B03C244S02H02: Duryodhana sets off for his capital in shame and despair, and Yudhishthira stays in the Dwaita woods, honoured by the Brahmanas.

B03C245.summary: Janamejaya asks how the humbled and shamed Duryodhana entered Hastinapura. Vaisampayana describes his slow departure and camp, and at night Karna comes to him, congratulating him on his survival and on the brothers' victory. Karna admits that he himself fled the battle, and Duryodhana answers in tears.

scenes.B03C245S01: Janamejaya asks about Duryodhana's shameful return, Duryodhana leaves in grief, and Karna comes to comfort him at night, admitting his own flight.

shots.B03C245S01H01: Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana to describe how the proud and shamed Duryodhana entered his capital after his defeat and rescue.
shots.B03C245S01H02: Duryodhana sets out in shame, camps, and at night Karna congratulates him on his survival and the brothers' victory, while admitting he himself fled the battle.
shots.B03C245S01H03: Vaisampayana says Duryodhana replied to Karna in a voice choked with tears.

B03C246.summary: Duryodhana tells Karna that the Gandharvas overpowered them with illusions and took them captive through the sky. He says that when his soldiers appealed to the Pandavas, Yudhishthira ordered them to free the captives, and that Chitrasena then made peace with Arjuna.

scenes.B03C246S01: Duryodhana explains to Karna how the Gandharvas captured the Kauravas, how the Pandavas freed them at the soldiers' appeal, and how Chitrasena reconciled with Arjuna.

shots.B03C246S01H01: Duryodhana tells Karna that the Gandharvas, using illusions, captured the Kauravas, that the soldiers appealed to the Pandavas, and that Yudhishthira ordered his brothers to free them, after which Chitrasena and Arjuna embraced and the Gandharvas laid down their arms.

B03C247.summary: Duryodhana recounts how Arjuna asked Chitrasena to free the Kaurava brothers, and how Chitrasena revealed their plan to mock the Pandavas. Overcome with shame, Duryodhana resolves to fast to death rather than return to the city, and offers the kingship to Dussasana, who weeps and refuses. Karna then urges the brothers to stop weeping, since the Pandavas were only doing their duty, and to return home.

scenes.B03C247S01: Duryodhana, ashamed of his captivity, resolves to starve himself, offers the throne to Dussasana, who refuses, and Karna urges the brothers to stop grieving and go home.

shots.B03C247S01H01: Duryodhana recalls how Chitrasena revealed their plan to mock the Pandavas, how they were handed over in chains, and, in shame, resolves to fast to death rather than return to his city.
shots.B03C247S01H02: Duryodhana offers the kingship to Dussasana, who refuses in tears and begs him to relent, and Dussasana vows he will never rule without his brother.
shots.B03C247S01H03: Karna scolds the brothers for weeping, says the Pandavas were only doing their duty, and urges Duryodhana to return to the city and console his brothers.

B03C248.summary: Karna argues that it is no shame that the Pandavas rescued Duryodhana, since subjects should serve their king and the Pandavas were bound to help him. He warns that a king who starves himself would be mocked by other kings, but Duryodhana is firm in his resolve and will not rise.

scenes.B03C248S01: Karna urges Duryodhana to rise and stop grieving, warning that a self-starving king would be mocked, and Duryodhana remains resolved to die.

shots.B03C248S01H01: Karna calls Duryodhana's grief childish, says the Pandavas were bound to rescue him as subjects of the king, urges him to rise, and warns that self-starvation would make him a laughing-stock.
shots.B03C248S01H02: Vaisampayana says Duryodhana, firmly resolved to leave the world, would not rise from where he sat.

B03C249.summary: Sakuni tries to rouse Duryodhana from his resolve to starve himself, urging him to return the kingdom to the Pandavas and make peace. Duryodhana refuses every counsel, and his friends say they cannot enter the city without him. The Danavas, who fear the loss of their ally, use a fire rite to summon him, and a goddess carries him off to the nether world, where he is flattered.

scenes.B03C249S01: Sakuni and the others fail to change Duryodhana's mind about fasting, and the Danavas summon him through a rite to their nether world, where they flatter him.

shots.B03C249S01H01: Sakuni tells Duryodhana that Karna's words are wise, that his grief is foolish, and urges him to return the kingdom to the Pandavas and make peace.
shots.B03C249S01H02: Duryodhana, seeing Dussasana lying prostrate in grief, refuses all counsel and resolves to die by fasting.
shots.B03C249S01H03: His friends reply that they will not enter the city without him.
shots.B03C249S01H04: Duryodhana spreads kusa grass, sits down in rags, and begins his fast in silent prayer.
shots.B03C249S01H05: The Danavas, fearing that Duryodhana's death would weaken them, hold a fire rite, and a goddess carries the king to the nether world, where the Danavas flatter him.

B03C250.summary: The Danavas urge Duryodhana to give up his fast, telling him he is of celestial origin and will be aided by demon-possessed warriors. They promise that Karna, possessed by the soul of Naraka, and the Samsaptakas will slay Arjuna. Duryodhana, believing it was a dream, returns to his army, and Karna encourages him to rise and vow to subdue the Pandavas.

scenes.B03C250S01: The Danavas promise Duryodhana victory, the goddess returns him to his place, and Karna urges him to rise and march back to the city with his army.

shots.B03C250S01H01: The Danavas urge Duryodhana to give up his fast, saying he is of celestial origin, that demon-possessed warriors will side with him, and that Karna, possessed by the soul of Naraka, and the Samsaptakas will slay Arjuna.
shots.B03C250S01H02: The Danavas embrace Duryodhana and send him back, where he takes it all for a dream, and the Danavas' influence makes Bhishma, Drona and Kripa less friendly to the Pandavas.
shots.B03C250S01H03: Karna urges Duryodhana to rise and vows to defeat Arjuna within thirteen years, and Duryodhana rises and marches with his army back to the city.

B03C251.summary: Janamejaya asks what the Kauravas did while the Pandavas lived in the forest. Bhishma rebukes Duryodhana for going to the forest, and advises peace with the Pandavas. Duryodhana laughs at his advice, and Karna boasts he will conquer the earth alone and humble Bhishma.

scenes.B03C251S01: Bhishma rebukes Duryodhana and urges peace, Duryodhana laughs at him, and Karna offers to conquer the earth alone, which Duryodhana welcomes.

shots.B03C251S01H01: Janamejaya asks what the sons of Dhritarashtra, Karna, Sakuni, Bhishma, Drona and Kripa did while the Pandavas lived in the forest.
shots.B03C251S01H02: Bhishma rebukes Duryodhana for his journey to the forest and his capture, notes that Karna fled from the Gandharvas, and urges peace with the Pandavas.
shots.B03C251S01H03: Duryodhana laughs and walks off, Bhishma goes home ashamed, and Karna vows to conquer the earth alone and show Bhishma his might.
shots.B03C251S01H04: Duryodhana is delighted by Karna's vow, and Karna sets out on an auspicious day with a rattling chariot that fills the three worlds with noise.

B03C252.summary: Karna sets out on a campaign of conquest, subduing Drupada, the northern and Himalayan kings, the eastern and southern lands, and the Yavana kings in the west. He returns to Hastinapura with great tribute, and Duryodhana honours him with praise. The city is divided in its response, and Karna then bows to Dhritarashtra and Gandhari, who embrace him, and the Kuru princes begin to believe the Pandavas already defeated.

scenes.B03C252S01: Karna conquers the kingdoms around, returns to Hastinapura with tribute, and is embraced by Dhritarashtra, who then trusts that the Pandavas have been defeated.

shots.B03C252S01H01: Karna besieges Drupada's city, forces him to pay tribute, and then conquers the north, the east, the south and the west, including the Yavanas, before returning to Hastinapura, where Duryodhana honours him.
shots.B03C252S01H02: The city erupts in comment, some praising Karna and some censuring him, and after Karna bows to Dhritarashtra and Gandhari, who embrace him, Duryodhana and Sakuni begin to think the Pandavas already beaten.

B03C253.summary: Karna tells Duryodhana that the earth is now free of enemies, and Duryodhana proposes to hold the Rajasuya sacrifice that the Pandavas performed. The priest refuses, since Yudhishthira and Dhritarashtra are still alive, and suggests the Vaishnava sacrifice instead, to be ploughed with gold tribute. Duryodhana agrees, and craftsmen begin to make the sacrificial plough.

scenes.B03C253S01: Karna and Duryodhana plan a great sacrifice, the priests advise a different rite, and the work on the sacrificial plough begins.

shots.B03C253S01H01: Karna tells Duryodhana that the earth is rid of enemies, and urges him to rule it like Indra.
shots.B03C253S01H02: Duryodhana says he wishes to hold the Rajasuya sacrifice that the Pandavas performed, and Karna urges him to summon the Brahmanas and gather the materials.
shots.B03C253S01H03: The priest refuses the Rajasuya, since Yudhishthira and Dhritarashtra are alive, and proposes the Vaishnava sacrifice, to be ploughed with gold from the tribute.
shots.B03C253S01H04: Duryodhana and his brothers agree, and the king orders craftsmen to build the sacrificial plough.

B03C254.summary: Duryodhana's sacrifice begins with its rites, with Dhritarashtra, Vidura, Bhishma and Karna delighted. Dussasana sends a messenger to the Pandavas in the Dwaita forest to invite them. Yudhishthira declines to attend until his vow ends, and Bhima answers with a threat against Duryodhana, while Vidura entertains the guests.

scenes.B03C254S01: The sacrifice begins, Dussasana's messenger invites the Pandavas, Yudhishthira declines, and Vidura entertains the guests.

shots.B03C254S01H01: The sacrifice begins with its rites, and Dussasana sends a messenger to the Pandavas in the Dwaita forest to invite them to witness it.
shots.B03C254S01H02: Yudhishthira says he cannot attend until his vow of exile ends, Bhima answers with a threat against Duryodhana, and Vidura looks after the many guests who arrive.

B03C255.summary: After the sacrifice, the citizens praise Duryodhana, and Karna vows that he will not wash his feet or eat meat until he has slain Arjuna. Spies bring word of this vow to the Pandavas, who grow anxious and resolve to leave the Dwaita woods. Meanwhile Duryodhana rules the earth with his brothers and his elders, giving gifts to Brahmanas.

scenes.B03C255S01: The citizens praise the sacrifice, Karna vows to kill Arjuna, and Duryodhana rules and gives gifts, while the Pandavas grow anxious and plan to leave.

shots.B03C255S01H01: The citizens praise Duryodhana's sacrifice, some compare it unfavourably with Yudhishthira's, and Karna vows he will not wash his feet or eat meat until he has slain Arjuna.
shots.B03C255S01H02: Spies report Karna's vow to kill Arjuna, the Pandavas grow anxious, and Yudhishthira resolves to leave the Dwaita woods.
shots.B03C255S01H03: Duryodhana rules with his brothers and his elders, giving generously to Brahmanas, because he believes that giving and enjoying are the only uses of wealth.

B03C256.summary: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did in the forest after rescuing Duryodhana. Yudhishthira dreams that the surviving deer, the last of their herd, plead with him to leave the forest. Moved by pity, he resolves to take his brothers to the Kamyaka forest.

scenes.B03C256S01: Yudhishthira dreams of the surviving deer begging him to leave, and he moves the Pandavas to the Kamyaka forest out of pity.

shots.B03C256S01H01: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did in the forest after Duryodhana was rescued.
shots.B03C256S01H02: Yudhishthira dreams that the surviving deer ask him to leave the forest, he is moved by pity, and the Pandavas set out for the Kamyaka forest near Lake Trinavindu.

B03C257.summary: The Pandavas spend eleven years in misery, and Yudhishthira blames himself for their suffering. The sage Vyasa visits and teaches that happiness and sorrow alternate and that asceticism, truth and self-control bring merit. Yudhishthira asks whether charity or asceticism is greater, and Vyasa answers that charity is the harder discipline, then tells the story of Mudgala.

scenes.B03C257S01: The Pandavas endure their exile, Vyasa visits and teaches on asceticism, and then Yudhishthira asks about charity, leading Vyasa to tell the tale of Mudgala.

shots.B03C257S01H01: The Pandavas spend eleven years in misery, and Yudhishthira, blaming himself for their suffering, cannot sleep, while the brothers are changed by rage and hope.
shots.B03C257S01H02: The sage Vyasa visits, and seeing his grandsons thin and wasted in the forest, teaches that happiness and sorrow alternate and that asceticism and virtue bring merit.
shots.B03C257S01H03: Yudhishthira asks which practice is more fruitful in the next world, charity or asceticism.
shots.B03C257S01H04: Vyasa says charity is the hardest discipline, that even a small gift given purely is greatly rewarded, and begins the story of Mudgala's gift of a drona of corn.

B03C258.summary: Yudhishthira asks why and to whom Mudgala gave a drona of corn, and Vyasa describes Mudgala as a sage who lives by gleaning and feeds his guests generously. The fierce sage Durvasa comes repeatedly to test him, and Mudgala stays calm and generous each time. A celestial chariot then arrives to take Mudgala to heaven, and he asks the messenger about its pleasures and drawbacks before going.

scenes.B03C258S01: The story of Mudgala: his generous gift of corn, Durvasa's repeated tests, and the celestial chariot that comes to take him to heaven.

shots.B03C258S01H01: Yudhishthira asks why and to whom Mudgala gave a drona of corn, and what makes a life bear fruit.
shots.B03C258S01H02: Vyasa describes Mudgala, a sage in Kurukshetra who lives by gleaning and feeds his guests, whose grain multiplies with each pure gift.
shots.B03C258S01H03: The fierce sage Durvasa visits Mudgala repeatedly, eating his food and smearing himself with the leftovers, but Mudgala stays calm, generous and steady.
shots.B03C258S01H04: A celestial messenger arrives with a swan-drawn chariot and tells Mudgala that he has earned his place in heaven.
shots.B03C258S01H05: Mudgala asks the messenger about the austerities, purposes and pleasures of heaven and what drawbacks it has before he ascends.

B03C259.summary: The celestial messenger describes the splendours of heaven, but also its drawbacks: one must exhaust one's merit and fall back, with regret and fear. Mudgala rejects heaven and asks for a region free from such faults, and the messenger describes the supreme seat of Vishnu, which Mudgala attains in liberation. Vyasa then consoles Yudhishthira, telling him that the kingdom will return after the thirteenth year, and goes back to his hermitage.

scenes.B03C259S01: The messenger describes heaven and its drawbacks, Mudgala chooses liberation over heaven, and Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira and departs.

shots.B03C259S01H01: The messenger describes the bliss of heaven, its regions and gardens, and the higher worlds of Brahma and the Ribhus, where desire and grief are absent.
shots.B03C259S01H02: The messenger describes the drawbacks of heaven, where one must exhaust one's merit and then fall, with regret and fear.
shots.B03C259S01H03: Mudgala rejects heaven, the messenger describes Vishnu's supreme seat, and Mudgala attains liberation; Vyasa then tells Yudhishthira that happiness and misery alternate and that his kingdom will return after thirteen years.
shots.B03C259S01H04: Vaisampayana says Vyasa went back to his hermitage to perform austerities.

B03C260.summary: Janamejaya asks how Duryodhana treated the Pandavas in the forest. Duryodhana, hearing they live happily there, plots harm with Karna and Dussasana, and Durvasa arrives with ten thousand disciples to test the prince, who serves him patiently. Duryodhana asks the sage to visit Yudhishthira after Draupadi has eaten, and the conspirators celebrate the plan.

scenes.B03C260S01: Duryodhana plots against the Pandavas, Durvasa tests and then favours him, and Duryodhana asks him to visit the Pandavas after Draupadi has eaten.

shots.B03C260S01H01: Janamejaya asks how Duryodhana and his counsellors treated the Pandavas in the forest.
shots.B03C260S01H02: Duryodhana plots against the Pandavas with Karna and Dussasana, and Durvasa arrives with ten thousand disciples and tests the prince, who serves him patiently.
shots.B03C260S01H03: Duryodhana asks Durvasa to visit Yudhishthira after Draupadi has eaten, and the sage agrees, while Karna and the prince rejoice that the Pandavas will suffer.
shots.B03C260S01H04: Duryodhana and his companions return home, pleased with their scheme.

B03C261.summary: Durvasa arrives at the Pandavas' hermitage after Draupadi has already eaten, and Yudhishthira asks him to return after his bath. Draupadi, anxious about the missing food, prays to Krishna, who appears, eats the last grain left in the sun-given vessel, and sends Bhima to invite the sages. The sages, filled up and fearing the Pandavas' wrath, flee, and Krishna reassures the Pandavas before departing.

scenes.B03C261S01: Durvasa visits the Pandavas when Draupadi has eaten; she prays to Krishna, who eats the last grain, and the sages flee, leaving the Pandavas safe.

shots.B03C261S01H01: A heading naming the section as the Draupadi-harana Parva.
shots.B03C261S01H02: Durvasa arrives with ten thousand disciples at a time when Draupadi has eaten, and Yudhishthira welcomes him and asks him to return after his bath.
shots.B03C261S01H03: Draupadi, worried that no food is left, prays to Krishna, who comes, eats the last grain stuck to the sun-given vessel, and sends Bhima to invite the sages.
shots.B03C261S01H04: The sages, feeling full after bathing, fear the Pandavas' wrath and flee, and Krishna appears to tell the Pandavas they need not fear Durvasa.
shots.B03C261S01H05: The Pandavas, relieved, thank Krishna, who departs for his capital, while they continue their wanderings with Draupadi, and the Kauravas' plot is defeated.

B03C262.summary: The Pandavas hunt in the Kamyaka forest, leaving Draupadi alone at the hermitage. Jayadratha, king of Sindhu, on his way to seek a bride in Salwa, sees her and is seized with desire, and he sends his companion Kotika to find out who she is.

scenes.B03C262S01: The Pandavas hunt in Kamyaka, Jayadratha sees Draupadi at the hermitage, and he sends Kotika to ask who she is.

shots.B03C262S01H01: The Pandavas hunt in the Kamyaka forest, leaving Draupadi alone at the hermitage, when Jayadratha sees her, is struck with desire, and sends Kotika to ask who she is.

B03C263.summary: Kotika approaches Draupadi, asks who she is and where her family comes from, and introduces himself as Suratha's son. He names his companions, including Kshemankara of Trigarta and Jayadratha, king of Sauvira, who is nearby with a large army, and asks Draupadi to say whose wife and daughter she is.

scenes.B03C263S01: Kotika asks Draupadi who she is and introduces himself and the princes with him, naming Jayadratha of Sauvira as their leader.

shots.B03C263S01H01: Kotika asks Draupadi who she is, guesses at divine origins, and names his companions, including Kshemankara of Trigarta and Jayadratha of Sauvira, with his chariots and standard-bearers.

B03C264.summary: Draupadi answers Kotika, saying that although it is not proper for a woman to speak to a stranger alone, she will introduce herself. She is Drupada's daughter and the wife of the five Pandavas, who have gone hunting in the four directions, and she invites the visitors to dismount and await a welcome from her husbands. She then enters her cottage.

scenes.B03C264S01: Draupadi introduces herself and her husbands, who are away hunting, and invites the visitors to wait for their hospitality before she withdraws.

shots.B03C264S01H01: Draupadi answers Kotika, introduces herself as Drupada's daughter and the wife of the five Pandavas, who have gone hunting in the four directions, and invites the visitors to dismount and wait to be welcomed.

B03C265.summary: Kotika reports the encounter to Jayadratha, who is captivated by Draupadi and resolves to make her his own. Kotika tells him she is Drupada's daughter and the Pandavas' wife, but Jayadratha is undeterred. Jayadratha then goes to the hermitage himself and presses his suit.

scenes.B03C265S01: Kotika tells Jayadratha who Draupadi is, Jayadratha is captivated and goes to the hermitage, and he urges her to abandon the Pandavas and marry him.

shots.B03C265S01H01: Kotika tells Jayadratha that the lady is Drupada's daughter and the wife of the five Pandavas, and Jayadratha, captivated, tells him to take her to Sauvira.
shots.B03C265S01H02: Jayadratha enters the hermitage, and after Draupadi offers him food and a seat, he urges her to abandon the ruined Pandavas and share his kingdoms of Sindhu and Sauvira.
shots.B03C265S01H03: Draupadi withdraws with contempt, warns him sharply to be careful, and waits for her husbands to return.

B03C266.summary: Draupadi denounces Jayadratha in fury and warns that the Pandavas will destroy him. When he seizes her and drags her toward his chariot, she struggles and calls upon Dhaumya, who warns Jayadratha that he will pay for the deed. Dhaumya then follows the ravisher's army as Draupadi is carried away.

scenes.B03C266S01: Draupadi rebukes Jayadratha, refuses his demands, is seized and dragged to his chariot, and Dhaumya follows the ravisher's army.

shots.B03C266S01H01: Draupadi, furious, rebukes Jayadratha for insulting the Pandavas and compares his folly to provoking lions and venomous snakes.
shots.B03C266S01H02: Jayadratha replies that he is not frightened, that his clan is noble, and orders Draupadi onto his chariot or to beg mercy of the Sauvira king.
shots.B03C266S01H03: Draupadi replies that Arjuna, Bhima and the Vrishni and Andhaka warriors will come after her, and that Jayadratha will have cause to regret his deed.
shots.B03C266S01H04: Jayadratha seizes Draupadi, who pushes him down and calls for Dhaumya, and the ravisher drags her to his chariot, while Dhaumya warns that he will pay for this deed.
shots.B03C266S01H05: Dhaumya follows the ravisher's infantry as Draupadi is carried off.

B03C267.summary: The Pandavas return from hunting, and Yudhishthira reads omens of trouble in the forest, including a jackal's cry that suggests the Kurus have turned to violence. At the hermitage they find Draupadi's maid weeping, and she tells them that Jayadratha has carried Draupadi off and urges them to pursue at once. Yudhishthira bids her be silent, and the brothers follow the tracks, rushing to rescue her.

scenes.B03C267S01: The Pandavas return to find Draupadi's maid weeping, learn that Jayadratha has carried her off, and follow the tracks in pursuit.

shots.B03C267S01H01: The Pandavas return from hunting, Yudhishthira reads omens of an invasion, and at the hermitage Draupadi's maid Dhatreyika tells Indrasena that Jayadratha has carried Draupadi away, urging them to pursue.
shots.B03C267S01H02: Yudhishthira tells the maid to be silent, warning that princes and kings who are drunk with power come to grief.
shots.B03C267S01H03: The brothers follow the tracks, see the dust of Jayadratha's army and Dhaumya among the infantry, and rush at the enemy in fury, causing them to lose their bearings.

B03C268.summary: Jayadratha, seeing the Pandava banners, asks Draupadi to name her husbands. She describes each brother, from Yudhishthira's virtue to Bhima's vengeance, Arjuna's steadiness and the twins' gifts, and warns that Jayadratha will be destroyed. The five brothers then fall on the enemy charioteers, darkening the air with arrows.

scenes.B03C268S01: Jayadratha asks Draupadi to name the Pandavas, she describes each brother and warns him, and the brothers attack the enemy charioteers.

shots.B03C268S01H01: Jayadratha asks Draupadi to name her husbands, and she describes each Pandava, from Yudhishthira's virtue to Bhima's vengeance, Arjuna's skill and the twins' gifts, and warns that his men will not survive.
shots.B03C268S01H02: The five brothers, enraged, leave the panic-stricken infantry and attack the charioteers, darkening the air with a thick shower of arrows.

B03C269.summary: The Pandavas attack Jayadratha's army and slaughter many of its warriors, though Yudhishthira is wounded, and Jayadratha flees, leaving Draupadi behind. Bhima wants to pursue and kill him, but Yudhishthira asks him to spare the king for the sake of their sister Dussala. Draupadi urges her husbands to slay the wretch, and the brothers set off after him.

scenes.B03C269S01: The Pandavas rout the Sindhu army and Jayadratha flees, Yudhishthira asks Bhima to spare him, and Draupadi urges the brothers to pursue and slay him.

shots.B03C269S01H01: The Pandavas attack the Sindhu army and cut down its warriors, Yudhishthira is wounded and his horses slain, Jayadratha flees leaving Draupadi behind, and Arjuna urges Bhima to seek Jayadratha instead of slaughtering the rest.
shots.B03C269S01H02: Bhima vows he will not let Jayadratha live, and Yudhishthira asks him to spare the king for the sake of their sister Dussala and Gandhari.
shots.B03C269S01H03: Draupadi, incensed, urges Bhima and Arjuna to slay the mean wretch, and the brothers go in search of him, while Yudhishthira returns to the hermitage with Draupadi.
shots.B03C269S01H04: Arjuna kills Jayadratha's horses and overtakes the fleeing king, rebuking him for his cowardice, and Bhima catches up with him, though Arjuna asks that he not be killed.

B03C270.summary: Bhima seizes Jayadratha, humiliates him, and forces him to declare himself a slave of the Pandavas, and Yudhishthira then frees him with a rebuke. Jayadratha, seeking revenge, obtains a boon from Shiva that he may check the Pandavas for a single day, except Arjuna. Shiva explains Arjuna's divine powers and recounts Vishnu's incarnations, and then vanishes with Uma while Jayadratha returns home.

scenes.B03C270S01: Bhima humiliates Jayadratha and Yudhishthira frees him; Jayadratha seeks Shiva's boon, and Shiva recounts Vishnu's incarnations and Arjuna's divine powers.

shots.B03C270S01H01: Bhima seizes Jayadratha, humiliates him, and forces him to declare himself a slave of the Pandavas, and Yudhishthira frees him with a rebuke, after which Jayadratha obtains a limited boon from Shiva, who explains Arjuna's divine power and recounts Vishnu's incarnations.
shots.B03C270S01H02: Shiva vanishes with Uma from the place, and the wicked Jayadratha returns home, while the Pandavas continue to dwell in the forest of Kamyaka.

B03C271.summary: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did after Draupadi's abduction. Yudhishthira, having rescued her, asks the sage Markandeya whether anyone has suffered as much as he and his brothers have, given the innocence of Draupadi and the trials of their exile.

scenes.B03C271S01: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did next, and Yudhishthira asks Markandeya whether any man has suffered more than he has.

shots.B03C271S01H01: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did after Draupadi's abduction.
shots.B03C271S01H02: Yudhishthira asks Markandeya whether anyone has suffered as he has, noting that Draupadi was innocent, that Jayadratha was punished, and that their life in the forest is full of hardship.

B03C272.summary: Markandeya tells Yudhishthira that Rama also suffered when Ravana carried off his wife Sita, and that Rama recovered her with Sugriva's help. Yudhishthira asks about Rama's birth, his might, and Ravana's ancestry and quarrel with him. Markandeya begins the tale with Rama's royal family and the origins of Sita and Ravana.

scenes.B03C272S01: Markandeya describes Rama's loss of Sita, Yudhishthira asks about Rama's family, and Markandeya begins the story of Rama's and Ravana's origins.

shots.B03C272S01H01: Markandeya says that Rama also suffered when Ravana carried off Sita, and that Rama recovered her with Sugriva's help, bridging the sea and burning Lanka.
shots.B03C272S01H02: Yudhishthira asks Markandeya about Rama's family and might, and about Ravana's ancestry and quarrel with Rama.
shots.B03C272S01H03: Markandeya begins the tale, naming Rama's royal line and his brothers, and then tells of the birth of Sita and of Ravana's ancestors, Pulastya and Visrava.

B03C273.summary: Markandeya tells how the Rishi Visrava's three Rakshasa wives bear him sons, including Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Vibhishana. The brothers perform severe penances, and Brahma grants Ravana protection from all beings except men and grants Vibhishana immortality for his righteousness. Ravana then defeats his half-brother Kubera, takes Lanka and the Pushpaka chariot, and earns the name Ravana for terrorising the world.

scenes.B03C273S01: Visrava's sons perform penances, Brahma grants them boons, and Ravana defeats Kubera, takes Lanka and the Pushpaka chariot, and comes to terrorise the world.

shots.B03C273S01H01: Visrava's Rakshasa wives bear him sons, including Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Vibhishana, Khara and Surpanakha, and Ravana's penance wins Brahma's promise that only men may harm him.
shots.B03C273S01H02: Brahma grants Kumbhakarna long sleep and Vibhishana immortality, because Vibhishana's soul is inclined to righteousness even though he was born a Rakshasa.
shots.B03C273S01H03: Ravana defeats Kubera, takes Lanka and the Pushpaka chariot, and Kubera curses him that the chariot will bear the man who slays him.
shots.B03C273S01H04: Vibhishana follows Kubera and is given command of the Yakshas and Rakshasas, while Ravana, granted supremacy by the Rakshasas, attacks the gods and Daityas and earns the name Ravana for terrifying all creatures.

B03C274.summary: The sages, gods and Siddhas, led by Agni, beg Brahma to protect them from Ravana, who cannot be killed because of his boon. Brahma replies that Ravana's death is near and that Vishnu will incarnate to achieve it. He then orders the gods to beget monkey and bear sons as Vishnu's allies, and sends a Gandharva woman to be reborn as the hunchback Manthara to stir up trouble.

scenes.B03C274S01: The gods and sages seek Brahma's help against Ravana, Brahma foretells Vishnu's incarnation, and he orders the gods to beget monkey and bear allies and sends Manthara to sow strife.

shots.B03C274S01H01: The sages and gods, led by Agni, beg Brahma to protect them from the Ten-headed Ravana, who cannot be slain by gods or demons because of his boon.
shots.B03C274S01H02: Brahma replies that Ravana's death is near, that he has arranged it, and that Vishnu will achieve it.
shots.B03C274S01H03: Brahma orders the gods to beget monkey and bear sons as Vishnu's allies, and sends a Gandharva woman to be born as the hunchback Manthara to stir up quarrels.

B03C275.summary: Yudhishthira asks why Rama, Lakshmana and Sita were sent into exile. Markandeya describes Rama's virtues and Dasaratha's plan to make him regent, which Kaikeyi's maid Manthara turns into a plot against Rama. Kaikeyi claims two boons, making her son Bharata king and sending Rama away for fourteen years, and Dasaratha dies of grief while Rama is in the forest.

scenes.B03C275S01: Yudhishthira asks about Rama's exile, Markandeya describes Dasaratha's plan and Kaikeyi's demands, the forest life and Dandaka battles, and Surpanakha's complaint to Ravana.

shots.B03C275S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Markandeya why Rama, Lakshmana and Sita went to the forest in exile.
shots.B03C275S01H02: Markandeya describes Rama's skill and virtues, and Dasaratha, pleased with his son, plans to install him as regent at an auspicious hour.
shots.B03C275S01H03: Kaikeyi's maid Manthara tells her mistress that Rama's coronation is a disaster for Bharata and that Kausalya will be the happy one.
shots.B03C275S01H04: Kaikeyi holds Dasaratha to his promise and demands that Bharata be made king and Rama exiled for fourteen years, Rama leaves with Lakshmana and Sita, Dasaratha dies, Bharata refuses the throne and rules with Rama's sandals, and Rama destroys the Rakshasas Khara and Dushana in Dandaka.
shots.B03C275S01H05: Surpanakha, her face mutilated, goes to Ravana, who vows revenge, and after making arrangements for his capital he flies to Gokarna to meet his old friend Maricha.

B03C276.summary: Ravana asks Maricha to help him by taking the form of a golden deer to lure Rama away from Sita. Maricha agrees, and Ravana disguises himself as an ascetic, while Rama and Lakshmana are drawn off in pursuit of the deer. Ravana seizes Sita, who refuses him, and flies off with her as the vulture Jatayu watches in distress.

scenes.B03C276S01: Ravana enlists Maricha, who lures Rama away in deer form; Sita is left alone, and Ravana abducts her while the vulture Jatayu watches.

shots.B03C276S01H01: Ravana visits Maricha, who warns him against Rama, but Ravana threatens him with death and orders him to lure Sita in the form of a golden deer.
shots.B03C276S01H02: Ravana disguises himself as an ascetic and Maricha as a deer; Sita sends Rama after it, Rama kills the Rakshasa, who cries out in Rama's voice, and Sita angrily sends Lakshmana to help.
shots.B03C276S01H03: Ravana, disguised as a hermit, approaches Sita, who refuses him, and he seizes her and flies off with her, while the vulture Jatayu watches.

B03C277.summary: The vulture Jatayu, a friend of Dasaratha, tries to free Sita from Ravana and is mortally wounded after his wings are cut off, while Sita drops her ornaments and cloth for her husband to find. Rama and Lakshmana return to find her gone, and the dying Jatayu points them south toward Ravana. They then kill a headless Rakshasa, who is revealed to be a Gandharva under a Brahmana's curse, and he directs them to seek Sugriva's friendship at Pampa.

scenes.B03C277S01: Jatayu fights Ravana and falls, Sita is carried to Lanka, and Rama and Lakshmana, searching for her, kill a headless Rakshasa who advises them to seek Sugriva.

shots.B03C277S01H01: The vulture Jatayu, a friend of Dasaratha, attacks Ravana to free Sita, is cut down when Ravana severs his wings, and Sita drops her ornaments and a cloth among five monkeys as Ravana flies to Lanka.
shots.B03C277S01H02: Rama returns, reproaches Lakshmana for leaving Sita, learns of her abduction, and finds the dying Jatayu, who points south; Rama and Lakshmana then slay a headless Rakshasa, who turns out to be a Gandharva cursed by a Brahmana and directs them to Sugriva at Pampa.

B03C278.summary: Rama, grieving for Sita, is roused by Lakshmana and goes to Rishyamuka, where he allies with Sugriva. Rama kills Vali from hiding and Sugriva takes back the monkey kingdom. In Lanka, Sita is held in an Asoka grove under guard, and Trijata comforts her with a message of hope and a dream of Ravana's fall. The section matters because it sets up the alliance that will carry the war against Ravana.

scenes.B03C278S01: Rama's journey to Pampa and Rishyamuka, his alliance with Sugriva and the killing of Vali, followed by Sita's state in Lanka and the comfort Trijata gives her.

shots.B03C278S01H01: Rama grieves at Pampa, Lakshmana rouses him, and the brothers reach Rishyamuka and make an alliance with Sugriva; Rama shoots Vali, Sugriva regains his kingdom and Tara, and Rama stays four months on the Malyavat hill.
shots.B03C278S01H02: Ravana keeps Sita in an Asoka grove guarded by Rakshasa women; she says she would rather die than live without Rama, and Trijata reassures her with a message that Rama is allied with Sugriva and will come, and with a dream of Ravana's downfall.
shots.B03C278S01H03: Heading marking the start of the next section, CCLXXIX.

B03C279.summary: Ravana comes to Sita in the Asoka grove, filled with desire, and boasts of his power, wealth and lineage to win her as his queen. Sita firmly refuses, saying she belongs to her husband and reproaching him for shaming his brother, the lord of treasures. Ravana vanishes, and Sita remains in grief under Trijata's care. The episode shows Sita's unbending loyalty to Rama and sets Ravana's pride against it.

scenes.B03C279S01: Ravana visits Sita in the grove, offers her the place of queen, and is refused by her before he goes away.

shots.B03C279S01H01: Ravana approaches Sita in the grove, lists his wealth, servants and descent and offers her the place of queen; Sita rejects him, cries, and reproaches him for disgracing his brother; Ravana vanishes, and Sita stays grieving with Trijata.

B03C280.summary: Rama, still longing for Sita, sends Lakshmana to remind Sugriva of his pledge, and Sugriva says his monkeys are searching the whole earth. The searchers in the north, east and west find nothing, but the southern party returns with news. Hanuman reports that he found Sita in Lanka and carried back a token from her. The section matters because it turns the search into a known location for Sita and sets up the march on Lanka.

scenes.B03C280S01: Lakshmana presses Sugriva to act, the search parties return, and Hanuman reports finding Sita in Ravana's city of Lanka.

shots.B03C280S01H01: Rama, awake on the hill and troubled by thoughts of Sita, sends Lakshmana to Kishkindhya to hold Sugriva to his word, and Sugriva replies that his monkeys are searching every land.
shots.B03C280S01H02: Lakshmana brings Sugriva back to Rama, the searchers from the north, east and west return empty-handed, and Rama keeps his hope on the southern party.
shots.B03C280S01H03: Hanuman tells how the southern party crossed a cave, met an ascetic woman, learned of Jatayu from his brother Sampati, and how Hanuman crossed the sea, found Sita in Lanka, gave her Rama's message, took a jewel from her as proof, and set fire to the city.

B03C282.summary: Ravana strengthens Lanka with trenches, stakes, catapults and armed guards. Angada delivers Rama's challenge in the king's court, and Ravana's men try to seize him, but he escapes and returns to Rama. The armies then clash at the walls: Rama's forces break down the ramparts and fight fiercely with the Rakshasas, and the monkeys withdraw after damaging the defenses. The section marks the outbreak of open war at Lanka.

scenes.B03C282S01: Ravana fortifies the city, Angada delivers Rama's challenge and escapes Ravana's men, and then the armies fight at Lanka's walls.

shots.B03C282S01H01: Rama's army settles in the groves, Ravana builds layered defenses around Lanka, and Angada enters, delivers Rama's defiant message, is seized by four Rakshasas, leaps free, and returns to Rama.
shots.B03C282S01H02: Rama's army breaks down the ramparts, Lakshmana breaches the southern gate, and the monkeys and bears swarm over the walls until the city's guards flee.
shots.B03C282S01H03: Ravana sends out Rakshasas in great numbers, the battle becomes fierce on the walls, Rama and Lakshmana shoot down many enemies, and the monkeys withdraw after damaging the city's defenses.

B03C281.summary: The monkey and bear armies gather around Rama and march to the southern sea. Since the sea is too wide to cross by boat, Rama prays to the Ocean, which agrees to let Nala's bridge carry the army across. Vibhishana, Ravana's brother, comes over to Rama and is made king of the Rakshasas. The army crosses to Lanka, and spies are caught and sent back, and Angada is sent as envoy to Ravana.

scenes.B03C281S01: The armies assemble and reach the sea, Rama asks the Ocean for a way across, and Nala builds a bridge that carries the army to Lanka; Vibhishana joins Rama, and Angada is sent to Ravana.

shots.B03C281S01H01: Monkey and bear chiefs gather from many regions, the army marches to the southern sea, and after Rama prays to the Ocean, the Ocean lets Nala build a bridge of floating materials that is still called Nala's bridge.
shots.B03C281S01H02: Vibhishana comes to Rama and is made king of the Rakshasas, the army crosses on the bridge and damages Lanka's gardens, two of Ravana's spies are seized and sent back, and Rama sends Angada to Ravana as envoy.

B03C283.summary: Ravana's lesser demons slip into the monkey camp invisibly, but Vibhishana sees through the spell and they are killed. Ravana then marches out in formation and the armies meet, with Rama, Lakshmana and others each matched against a chosen foe. The section marks the start of the full battle of Lanka.

scenes.B03C283S01: Ravana's invisible demons are exposed and killed, and Ravana opens a general battle in which the chief warriors on each side are paired off.

shots.B03C283S01H01: Ravana's lesser demons sneak into the monkey camp invisibly, Vibhishana breaks their spell, they are killed, and Ravana forms his army for a general battle in which Rama, Lakshmana, Sugriva and others each take on a chosen opponent.

B03C284.summary: Prahasta attacks Vibhishana with a mace, but Vibhishana kills him with an enchanted javelin. Dhumraksha then drives back the monkeys until Hanuman turns the fight and kills him. Ravana, grieving, wakes his sleeping brother Kumbhakarna and sends him into battle, with the younger brothers Vajravega and Promathin joining. The section shows Ravana's army losing its leaders and Ravana turning to his last strong warrior.

scenes.B03C284S01: Prahasta and Dhumraksha are killed, and Ravana wakes Kumbhakarna and sends him out to fight.

shots.B03C284S01H01: Prahasta is killed by Vibhishana, Hanuman defeats and kills Dhumraksha after the monkeys rally, and Ravana wakes Kumbhakarna and sends him, with Vajravega and Promathin, into battle.

B03C285.summary: Kumbhakarna devours several monkey leaders and seizes Sugriva, but Lakshmana wounds him with an arrow and cuts off his arms as they grow back. A Brahma weapon from Lakshmana finally kills him. Hanuman and Nala then kill Vajravega and Promathin, but the fighting goes on with heavy losses to the Rakshasas. The section records the fall of Ravana's strongest warrior.

scenes.B03C285S01: Kumbhakarna is struck down by Lakshmana, and his two younger brothers are killed by Hanuman and Nala, while the battle continues.

shots.B03C285S01H01: Kumbhakarna eats several monkey leaders and grabs Sugriva, until Lakshmana's arrows, the growing arms and a Brahma weapon bring him down, and then Hanuman and Nala kill his brothers Vajravega and Promathin.

B03C286.summary: Ravana, hearing of the deaths, sends his son Indrajit to end the war by killing Rama, Sugriva and Lakshmana. Indrajit challenges Lakshmana, and their duel goes back and forth until Angada wrecks Indrajit's chariot with a tree. Indrajit vanishes by illusion and shoots down Rama and Lakshmana. The section shows Indrajit's power of illusion as the main threat to the brothers.

scenes.B03C286S01: Ravana urges Indrajit to fight, Indrajit duels with Lakshmana and Angada, and then vanishes and wounds Rama and Lakshmana.

shots.B03C286S01H01: Ravana urges Indrajit to kill Rama, Sugriva and Lakshmana, Indrajit duels Lakshmana and Angada until Angada wrecks his chariot, and Indrajit vanishes by illusion and shoots Rama and Lakshmana until they fall.

B03C287.summary: Indrajit binds Rama and Lakshmana in a net of arrows, but Vibhishana revives them, and Sugriva's healing and a sacred water sent by Kuvera let them see the invisible. Indrajit returns to battle and Lakshmana kills him with three fiery arrows. Ravana, grieving, rushes to kill Sita, but Avindhya talks him out of it by urging him to kill Rama instead. The section shows Rama's side recovering and Ravana's rage turning toward Sita.

scenes.B03C287S01: Vibhishana revives the brothers, who gain sight of invisible beings, Lakshmana kills Indrajit, and Avindhya persuades Ravana to spare Sita and go to battle himself.

shots.B03C287S01H01: Indrajit binds the brothers in a net of arrows, Vibhishana revives them with a weapon, Sugriva pulls out the arrows with healing medicine, and Vibhishana gives them and the monkeys water from Kuvera that lets them see invisible creatures.
shots.B03C287S01H02: Indrajit returns and Lakshmana, guided by Vibhishana, kills him with three arrows and then kills his charioteer; Ravana, grieving, rushes at Sita with a sword, Avindhya argues him out of it, and Ravana sets out to fight.

B03C288.summary: Ravana, enraged by his son's death, attacks with illusory warriors that Rama's arrows overcome. Matali brings Indra's chariot, and Vibhishana assures Rama that it is real, so Rama rides out to face Ravana. After a long duel, Rama fires a Brahma weapon that burns Ravana and his chariot to nothing. The section marks the death of Ravana and the end of the war's central conflict.

scenes.B03C288S01: Ravana's illusions fail, Matali brings Indra's chariot to Rama, and Rama kills Ravana with a Brahma weapon.
